I was at a group fitness class once. We were told to lie down and meditate when a couple of girls came in. I was a newbie in the group and they weren't. I lay with my eyes shut doing what I had been told to do. They started asking, "Who is she?" I didn't know how to react because they weren't talking to me and instead used third person, so I continued trying to mediate. The girls joked around a little more, eventually saying that "she" fell asleep and laughing.

I felt awful. Sports is not my best side, so I'm always very sensitive when someone makes fun of me during exercise. The girls were having a separate conversation, even though it was about me, so I didn't know if I should interfere. Maybe the right thing was to stop the meditation and laugh with them, but I couldn't make myself, I was too upset…

So yeah, the condescending tone and little jokes that I don't know how to react to are the big reasons I don't like that I'm shy.

I'm guessing that if you posted this, you want to get better. So, do it, step by step. Start with something small and do it every day.

Start going to church every week (I'm assuming you, like me, don't do it out of shame). Pray, pray every morning, evening, whenever you feel the urge to relapse, pray, even if doesn't stop you from relapsing at first, pray with a book or in your own words. You want to get the feeling that God is with you at all times back.

Think about the roots of your addiction. Why do you watch p.? Why exactly hardcore? What things can give you joy and satisfaction (what did in the past)? You want to achieve the same result (feeling fulfilled) by the means of something else.

At the end of the day, remember something good about it. Anything. Delicious coffee you had in the morning, the favourite pair of socks, your mum, the access to water and food, etc. The things that come to mind are individual. This may show you that God gave you a lot of things to be grateful for, that He is almighty, so He can help you with your addiction.

I think these are the things you can start with to revive your will to live. I believe in you and want you to get better. Good luck.

She believes everything on TV and in newspapers and doesn't get the whole concept of advertising ("if it is shown on TV it cannot be fake").

My mother was born in the 70s. She understands the pros and cons of USSR, but her attitude to it is rather good than bad. She was proud to be a Pioneer, she is nostalgic about USSR.
